correctness.rationale: Every projective stabilizer element lifts along the birational normalization to an affine normalization automorphism, since the curve has a unique singular point with one preimage. The expanded three-section linear series forces \(b=0\) and \(a^{q+1}=1\) for \(q\ge4\), while cancellation at \(q=2\) gives \(a^3=1\) with free b. Explicit invertible matrices prove sufficiency and the reduced-group statements. Differentiation of F gives five independent monomial equations plus the scalar-projective quotient, yielding tangent dimension 3. Exact finite-field checks for \(q=2,4,8\) gave 12,5,9 stabilizers; generality is proved symbolically.

value.rationale: The exact stabilizer of an intrinsically motivated unicuspidal family answers a natural symmetry question left open by the initiating geometric construction. The answer is an all-degree classification with a sharp exceptional quartic boundary, and, more significantly, a uniform three-dimensional infinitesimal stabilizer contradicting the reduced symmetry dimension (zero in all higher degrees). This isolates a persistent characteristic-two group-scheme pathology that geometric-point calculations miss; it is neither a random parameter slice nor a numerical experiment.
